conversation.content:
Hi there—I’m so glad to meet you. I’m a clinician who specializes in caring for new mothers’ emotional health, and I’m here to make sure you feel supported as you navigate life with your baby.

Today I’ll be using a short questionnaire called the EPDS (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale). It’s simply a tool to help us understand how you’ve been feeling over the past week so we can be certain you’re getting any support you might need. Everything you share is confidential, and this is a judgment-free space—there are no right or wrong answers, only your experience.

We’ll go through ten gentle questions, one at a time, and you can answer in your own words. When you’re ready, we can begin.

Over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

I’ve noticed I don’t really laugh much anymore. My husband will make a joke or we’ll watch something that used to crack me up, and I might smile a little, but that real laugh just doesn’t bubble up the way it did before the baby. It feels like the joy is stuck behind a wall or something.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
No… I haven’t really been able to laugh. I might give a little smile if my husband tries to be funny, but it feels forced. Mostly I just feel flat, like the joy is stuck behind a wall or something.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I mean, I’ll still go meet a friend for coffee or put on a podcast I used to love, but the excited feeling I used to get beforehand just isn’t there. I do them more because I “should” than because I actually look forward to them.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. If the baby’s fussy and I can’t settle her right away, I’ll think, “I’m doing something wrong,” or “Other moms figure this out faster.” Even little things—like forgetting to bring a burp cloth—turn into, “I’m failing at this.” It’s not every second of the day, but it pops up a lot.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Most of the time, yeah. Like, I’ll lie in bed and suddenly imagine the baby’s blanket climbing up over her face, or worry that the little rash on her cheek is actually something awful. Nothing triggered it—I just can’t shut the thoughts off. I can usually talk myself down, but it keeps happening.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes, yeah. It’s not a full panic attack, but I’ll get this sudden rush—heart racing, chest tight—when I picture something happening to the baby or even just think about how I’m supposed to keep her safe every single second. It comes out of nowhere and fades after a few minutes, but it’s scary while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days feel like I’m juggling more than I can handle. I’ll be trying to feed her, the laundry’s piled up, the dog’s barking, and I just think, “I can’t do all this.” I still push through, but it’s like I’m constantly one step behind and about to drop everything.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Pretty often. I’ll lie down exhausted, but my head keeps spinning—going over everything I might have done wrong or imagining scary “what-ifs” about the baby. It takes me a long time to drift off, and then I wake up at two or three in the morning with the same worries racing.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I feel sad or empty a lot of the day. It’s not always crying-level sad—more like this heavy, gray cloud that follows me around. I’ll look at the baby and feel like I “should” be glowing, but instead I just feel flat and wonder if I’ll ever feel like myself again.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

A couple of times this week, yeah. Once was when she wouldn’t nap no matter what I tried—I just sat in the rocker with tears rolling down while she cried, too. Another night my partner asked how I was doing and the word “fine” came out wobbly and suddenly I was sobbing. It feels like the tears are right under the surface lately.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

Yeah… it’s crossed my mind once or twice, just a quick flash—like “what if I weren’t here” or thinking the baby might be better off without me. I haven’t made any plans or anything, and I’m scared by the thought, but it has popped in there.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 22: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary  
Date: [today]

Presenting symptoms  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, tearfulness  
- Marked loss of enjoyment in previously pleasurable activities  
- Daily guilt/self-blame re: mothering competence  
- Recurrent intrusive worries about infant safety; nocturnal rumination  
- Episodic panic-type sensations (racing heart, chest tightness) without clear trigger  
- Subjective overwhelm and sense of “falling behind”  
- Initial insomnia and middle-of-night re-awakening driven by anxious ruminations  
- Passive self-harm ideation (no plan, intent, or preparation reported)

Pattern  
Answers consistently reflect depressive cognitions and heightened anxiety beginning post-delivery; functional impact on sleep, coping, and emotional bonding.

Screening significance  
Scores indicate probable major depressive episode with anxious features; meets threshold for immediate safety assessment and possible referral for comprehensive evaluation.

Risk flags  
✓ Passive suicidal thoughts (“baby might be better off without me”)  
✓ Excessive guilt / feelings of maternal inadequacy  
✓ Panic-type symptoms and constant safety worries

Next step  
Discuss findings with patient; recommend same-day safety plan, support person notification, and expedited referral to perinatal mental health specialist for formal diagnostic interview and management.
